summary: The note previews a series of technology-focused health education events and workshops planned by local health organizations from September 2023 through March 2024. They cover VR mental health training, an AI nutrition app, fitness tech, gamification, telehealth, youth social media programs, a tech-themed health fair, e-learning, and sustainability. The overall theme is using digital tools to build health literacy and empower communities.
one_line: Local health organizations plan tech-driven health education workshops and events from September 2023 to March 2024 to boost community health literacy.
key_facts: The "Healthy Mind, Healthy Life" seminar is scheduled for September 15th and uses virtual reality (VR) to teach mental health and stress management; it is led by psychologist Dr. Emily Stiles.

The Green Leaf Health Consortium will unveil the "NutriGuide" app on October 3rd during National Nutrition Week; it uses AI to tailor meal plans and educational content, and is spearheaded by nutritionist Daniel Marks.

The week-long workshop "Future of Fitness: Embracing Technology for Better Health" runs November 6th to 12th and features celebrity trainer Jenna Caldwell, introducing wearable fitness trackers, smart gym equipment and online platforms.
The day-long "Gamify Your Health!" workshop on November 25th is headed by tech guru and gamer Alex Thompson, and attendees can beta-test new games promoting healthy habits and physical activity.

The "Telehealth in Your Neighborhood" series, organized by Local HealthNet, starts December 1st and teaches virtual consultations, remote monitoring devices and online health records; Elaine Peterson conducts the sessions.
The Healthy Youth Initiative starts its "Tech-Savvy Teens" program on December 15th, teaching adolescents health topics via social media and online forums.
Michael Borges, a social influencer and health advocate, leads the "Social Media for Social Good" workshop on health activism and positive self-image campaigns.

A community health fair on January 8, 2024 will have tech-centered booths with biometric screening devices and health advice chatbots; public health nurse Sarah McMillan will give live demonstrations.

LifeLong Health Advocates launches the e-learning course "Understanding Your Health: An E-Learning Journey" on February 10th, with modules on chronic disease management, first aid and preventative care; Dr. Luke Hendricks helped develop it.
The "Eco-Health Connection" workshop on March 12th focuses on sustainable health practices and is guided by environmental health expert Maya Singh.
The events are planned for after September 1, 2023.
